summary: Created AppCountryIDsValidation — custom BaseParamValidation that iterates each ID and produces a per-ID error message (VALIDATION_COUNTRY_ID_NOT_EXISTS = 184801) for any IDs that do not exist via AppFactory::createCountries()->idExists().
Created AppCountriesParamInterface — extends APIParameterInterface with getCountries(): Application_Countries_Country[], mirrors AppCountryParamInterface (singular) for pattern consistency.

Created AppCountryIDsParam — extends IDListParameter, implements AppCountriesParamInterface. Declares PARAM_COUNTRY_IDS = 'countryIDs' as its own constant (mirrors the soon-to-be-created AppCountriesAPIInterface constant). Constructor registers AppCountryIDsValidation. getCountries() guards against null getValue() and reuses a single createCountries() call.

Created AppCountryIDsHandler — extends BaseParamHandler with type-narrowed register() (ClassHelper::requireObjectInstanceOf), getParam() (instanceof guard), and createParam() overrides. resolveValueFromSubject() delegates to getParam()?->getCountries() ?? [].

comments.note: AppCountryIDsParam::getCountries() caches the AppFactory::createCountries() collection in a local variable and guards against null/empty getValue() before iterating. This avoids a repeated factory call per ID and prevents a TypeError on null. The plan's draft code called createCountries() inside the loop — the fix is low-effort but improves performance for large ID lists.

AppCountryIDsParam declares PARAM_COUNTRY_IDS = 'countryIDs' as its own constant rather than referencing AppCountriesAPIInterface::PARAM_COUNTRY_IDS (which doesn't exist until WP-003). Once WP-003 creates the interface, AppCountryIDsParam should be updated to remove the duplicate constant and reference the interface instead — or the param can remain self-contained and the interface can reference the param constant.

AppCountriesParamInterface references AppCountryISOsParam in its @see tag, but that class doesn't exist until WP-003. The @see annotation is forward-looking documentation and safe to leave; it should be verified once WP-003 is implemented.

comments.note: AppCountryIDsParam::getCountries() correctly calls AppFactory::createCountries() once before the foreach loop — improving on the plan's draft which called it inside the loop. This avoids repeated factory instantiation for large ID lists.

getCountries() calls Countries::getCountryByID() (non-nullable, throws on unknown ID). This is safe because AppCountryIDsValidation runs first and rejects any non-existent IDs — the ordering of validate-then-get is correct. However, if getCountries() were ever called manually (bypassing validation), it would throw. Acceptable given the intended usage contract.

summary: Reviewed all four WP-002 files line-by-line against maintainability, best practices, performance, and architectural alignment.

AppCountryIDsValidation: Clean, focused single-responsibility class. Short-circuits correctly on empty/null input before hitting the DB. Collects all invalid IDs before issuing one error (good UX — surfaces all failures at once rather than stopping at the first). The VALIDATION_COUNTRY_ID_NOT_EXISTS = 184801 constant is well-named and consistent with project conventions.

AppCountriesParamInterface: Minimal and correct. Correctly extends APIParameterInterface. The @see AppCountryISOsParam forward-reference is intentional (WP-003) and harmless — noted as documentation-forward for post-WP-003 verification.

AppCountryIDsParam: Correctly extends IDListParameter and implements AppCountriesParamInterface. The getCountries() guard (null || empty) is correct — IDListParameter.getValue() returns int[], not null, but the null guard is defensive and correct. The single AppFactory::createCountries() call before the loop is a meaningful performance improvement over the plan's draft. PARAM_COUNTRY_IDS constant duplication is by design (WP-003 will resolve it).

AppCountryIDsHandler: Faithfully follows and improves upon the AppCountryIDHandler (singular) pattern. The added PHPDoc on register(), getParam(), and resolveValueFromSubject() are a net improvement over the undocumented singular counterpart. The instanceof guard in getParam() is the correct narrowing idiom. createParam() is correct and minimal.
No blocking issues found. No Fix-Forward changes required. Two documentation-forward items recorded for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: AppCountryIDsHandler adds PHPDoc to resolveValueFromSubject(), register(), and getParam() — the singular AppCountryIDHandler has no docblocks on any of its methods. This is a measurable improvement to maintainability and sets a better pattern going forward.

AppCountryIDsValidation collects ALL invalid IDs into $invalid before issuing a single error. This is strictly better than failing on the first bad ID — consumers receive a complete list of what to fix in one round-trip. Good API design.

PARAM_COUNTRY_IDS = 'countryIDs' is declared on AppCountryIDsParam itself, as AppCountriesAPIInterface does not exist until WP-003. Once WP-003 is implemented, one of two resolutions should be applied: (a) AppCountryIDsParam removes its own constant and references AppCountriesAPIInterface::PARAM_COUNTRY_IDS, or (b) AppCountriesAPIInterface references AppCountryIDsParam::PARAM_COUNTRY_IDS to avoid circular dependency. Option (b) is preferable if the param class is the canonical owner. Track this in WP-003 scope.

[documentation-forward] AppCountriesParamInterface has a @see AppCountryISOsParam forward-reference that does not resolve until WP-003 is implemented. Verify the @see tag is accurate and points to the correct class once WP-003 is complete.

[documentation-forward] AppCountryIDsValidation PHPDoc explains why a custom validation class is needed over ValueExistsCallbackValidation (per-ID iteration). Consider adding a short note to the module-level README or API docs summarising validation strategy for multi-value parameters, so future contributors understand when to reach for BaseParamValidation vs the callback variant.
